verdict.rationale: First-party docs say Codex skills build on the open agent skills standard and use the standard skill shape: a directory with a `SKILL.md` that has `name` and `description` frontmatter, discovered from `.agents/skills`. A hands-on probe used third-party `npx skills` tooling to install a catalog skill as a plain folder with valid frontmatter, which corroborates that the format is not Codex-locked. Missing for 10: documented detail on which spec version or fields Codex conforms to (including any Codex-specific extensions), and hands-on evidence of the same skill folder running in another vendor's agent.

support.subject: As a developer, skills follow the open Agent Skills specification so the same skill folder is valid beyond this one vendor's tooling

citations.quote: Skills build on the open agent skills standard.
A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md` file plus optional scripts and references. The `SKILL.md` file must include `name` and `description`.
Codex scans `.agents/skills` in every directory from your current working directory up to the repository root.
the catalog's skills are plain portable folders that third-party tooling can install, not a Codex-locked format.
